who: Historian of British North America, University of New Brunswick from 2012; PhD Johns Hopkins, 1990.

evidence.says: UNB Archives identifies Elizabeth Mancke as a historian with a Johns Hopkins doctorate, joining UNB in 2012 and supervising over a dozen doctoral students.
The faculty listing records Elizabeth Mancke, assistant professor of history, with a Johns Hopkins PhD in 1990.
The candidate authority identifies Elizabeth Mancke as Canada Research Chair in Atlantic Canada Studies at UNB, citing Britain’s Oceanic Empire (2012).

notes: Name, university, field and doctorate agree. Later dissertation completion years do not establish the dates of supervision.

who: Peter R. Mansoor, military historian at Ohio State from 2008; PhD Ohio State, 1995.

evidence.says: Ohio State records Peter R. Mansoor’s history PhD in March 1995 and appointment to its military history chair in September 2008.
The authority names Peter R. Mansoor, associates him with Ohio State, and identifies The GI Offensive in Europe, also listed on his faculty page.

notes: Degree and appointment match the AHA record and cover the students’ 2016–2022 completion years.

who: Benjamin G. Rader, American historian at Nebraska–Lincoln; PhD Maryland, 1964.

evidence.says: The Benjamin G. Rader authority explicitly records a University of Maryland PhD in 1964 and teaching at Nebraska–Lincoln.
Nebraska identifies Benjamin Rader as former James L. Sellers Professor of History and emeritus professor.
Russ Crawford’s contributor biography states that he earned his Nebraska–Lincoln history PhD in 2004 under Benjamin Rader’s supervision.

notes: Exact doctorate match and direct confirmation of listed student Russ Crawford.

who: Nathan Stewart Rosenstein, historian of ancient Rome at Ohio State; PhD Berkeley, 1982.

evidence.says: Ohio State identifies Nathan Rosenstein as a Roman historian with a Berkeley PhD in 1982, and lists Imperatores Victi among his books.
The authority links Nathan Stewart Rosenstein and Nathan Rosenstein through the 1982 work The Forms and Limitation of Aristocratic Competition and Imperatores Victi (1990).
The department reports his retirement after 32 years at Ohio State and identifies Peter Vanderpuy (PhD 2017) as his advisee.

notes: Exact doctorate match; departmental evidence directly connects a listed student.

who: Daniel J. Sargent, historian of international and American history at Berkeley from 2008; PhD Harvard, 2008.

The Daniel J. Sargent authority identifies the Berkeley history professor and author of A Superpower Transformed, citing Oxford University Press.

who: Erik R. Seeman, early American historian at Buffalo from 1996; PhD Michigan, 1995.

evidence.says: Buffalo identifies Erik R. Seeman as a history professor with a Michigan PhD in 1995 and lists his early American history publications.
His institutional CV records Buffalo employment from 1996 and PhD committees chaired for all six listed students, with matching completion years.
The Seeman, Erik R. authority identifies the Buffalo history professor and author of Pious Persuasions and Speaking with the Dead in Early America.
Publisher-deposited metadata for Death in Early America identifies Erik R. Seeman, University at Buffalo (SUNY), with ORCID 0000-0002-1603-3371.

notes: The selected LC candidate p-3588 matches. The ORCID candidate p-12824 also matches through the article metadata; these appear to be duplicate graph records.

who: Roman Szporluk, historian of modern Eastern Europe at Harvard from 1991; PhD Stanford, 1965.

Harvard identifies Roman Szporluk as emeritus professor of Ukrainian history, researching modern Ukrainian, Russian and Polish history.
The candidate item identifies Roman Szporluk, lists Harvard and Michigan as employers, and links LC authority n79138736.

notes: Name, field, Stanford doctorate and Harvard appointment agree with the AHA record.

who: Richard A. Bartlett, historian of the American West at Florida State through 1989; PhD Colorado, 1953.

evidence.says: The Tallahassee Democrat obituary, linked by FSU’s history department, identifies Richard A. Bartlett, a Colorado PhD, as FSU history professor from the mid-1950s until 1989.
The bibliography cites R. A. Bartlett’s The Great Surveys in Colorado, 1867–1879 as a University of Colorado PhD dissertation, 1953.
The Richard A. Bartlett authority identifies the Florida State history professor and author of Great Surveys of the American West.
The alternative Richard H. Bartlett authority identifies a University of Western Australia law professor with a UWA PhD and works on mining and water law.

notes: p-125272 matches the institution, period, degree and field. Alternative p-137146 is a different scholar.
